results.title: World Transit Stops
results.description:
This layer depicts the public transportation stops received through the Esri Community Maps program, USDOT, and publicly available datasets from agencies, municipalities and countries around the world. It is designed to be used with the other World Transit layers in the Living Alas. These layers include:
  • World Transit Agency Centroids
  • World Transit Lines by Modality
  • World Transit Lines by Agency Color
     
These transit layers can be accessed together through the following resources:
  • World Transit Group Layer
  • World Transit Web Map
  • World Transit Viewer (Web Mapping Application)


Stops are symbolized by their modality, such as bus, train, or funicular. If a stop serves multiple modalities (a station with trains and busses), the stop symbology prioritizes more permanent modes of transport, such as train over bus. 

The transit data is received in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format, an open data standard for public transportation data. Each GTFS dataset is a zipped archive of comma-separated files describing the transit services, including the geometry for mapping. Esri converts GTFS datasets into ready-to-use map layers and makes them available as Feature Services in the Living Atlas. Esri Transit map layers include data from Esri Community Maps contributors, the US Department of Transportation, as well as publicly available GTFS datasets.
 
Please note that any data layer fields marked with an "(Esri)" tag have been added by Esri to provide user-friendly translations of GTFS standard values or to add additional context and value.

results.description:
Sun Metro Transit publicly available data of bus routes and bus stops across the City of El Paso.

 

Included in the bus routes are the numbered fixed route service, any peak service route deviations, as well as the BRIO and Streetcar routes. Included in the bus stops are the fixed route stops, the Streetcar stops, the bus terminal/transit/transfer center bay or platform locations, as well as the MicroTransit designated super stop locations.

 

These data are made available for public use. Datasets may not reflect all current service updates or changes and will not reflect dynamic service updates or changes (i.e., bus stop status or route deviations due to construction/road conditions, etc.).

(b) A ferry terminal served by either a bus or rail transit service.

(c) The intersection of two or more major bus routes with a frequency of service interval of 15 minutes or less during the morning and afternoon peak commute periods.

results.title: GTFS Transit Stops with Number of Stops Per Hour (Routes Combined)
results.description:
The General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) is a data specification that allows for transit agencies that operate fixed-route transit services to publish data related to routes, stops, and schedules. This layer is derived from regularly-updated assemblage of static GTFS data feeds from regional transit authorities in North Central Texas including DART, Trinity Metro, DCTA, and STAR. Additional layers and core GTFS tables are included in the map service that includes this layer.

For more information on the static "Schedule" GTFS, consult: https://gtfs.org/schedule/reference

This layer depicts stops dissolved into a single point per stop with metrics describing overall service frequency at that stop, regardless of route. Stops are located by provided coordinates, and may not necessarily intersect the routes they serve (i.e. offset from the street centerline). Every stop is represented by a single point with a field listing the routes serving it. The provided stops per hour metric is a sum of stops from all routes serving that stop. In cases where these fields are null, the stop may not be served by any routes during that time period.

results.title: PPACG Regional Transit Providers (2025)
results.description:
The Regional Transit Providers feature layer models the fixed-route bus and shuttle services operated by public, private, or nonprofit transit providers within the Pikes Peak Area Council of Governments (PPACG) region. The data in this feature class is developed by PPACG from information provided by or acquired from the region's transit providers, and updated in conjunction with the regional Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) and Long Range Transportation Plan (LRTP) development cycles.

This feature layer contains two traffic count layers:

Transit Service Stops

This layer models the stops operated by the regional transit providers. The 'StopNumID' field identifies the number or ID of each stop according to its service operator, while the 'StopName' field records either the name or the general location of each stop.

Transit Service Routes

This layer models the routes operated by the regional transit providers, and are typically adjusted to align with coincident Route Centerlines features to ensure spatial consistency with the regional roadway network. The 'Route_Name' field records the official name of each route according to its operator. The 'TrnSrvAvbl' field describes the general service availability of each route, such as weekday service, weekend service, both weekday and weekend service, or limited availability for services that only operate on select days.

Both layers include a 'Tran_Prvdr' field to record the entity which operates the fixed-route service, and a 'SrvYear' field to identity the operational year modeled by each feature. The remaining fields store data pertinent to PPACG's planning operations, and primarily describe the location, operational, and physical attributes of each stop.

The source of each feature's geometry and spatial definition is identified in the 'Geo_Source' field. The 'Geo_Edit' field describes any geometry edits that were made to alter the source data, such as adjustments to maintain consistency with neighboring data or imagery.

results.name: Transit_Stops
results.title: Transit Stops
results.description:
Abstract
The Transit Stops layer contains over 20,000 active and inactive transit stops in the Twin Cities seven county metropolitan area. The dataset includes attributes from the primary transit stop database maintained for Metro Transit and for customer information for other transit provider transit services. The locations are mapped referencing Road Centerlines (MN GAC standard) network along with streets generated internally at Metro Transit.

Data Quality
Attribute Accuracy: Attributes randomly checked by Metro Transit staff.

Completeness: All active and inactive transit stops. Does not include all retired stops.

Horizontal Positional Accuracy: Positional accuracy reflects stops and their association with the street centerline network.

Coordinate System
Horizontal Coordinate Scheme: Universal Transverse Mercator

UTM Zone Number: 15

Horizontal Datum: NAD83

Horizontal Units: meters

Attributes
Overview: PLEASE NOTE: HASTUS is the schedule-maker software that Metro Transit uses to manage routes and stops.

side_id: The primary key field and unique stop identification number assigned by Metro Transit.

site_on: The street or address where the stop is found.

site_at: The cross street or address nearest the stop.

CornerNumber: Unique id for corner location description that is used to locate a stop at an intersection by defining the direction of travel on the street where the stop is located and the stop's relationship to the nearest cross street.

corn_desc: The description of the corner the bus stop is on.

city: The city the stop is located in.

county: The county where the stop is located in.

publiccomm: Miscellaneous oomments about the stop.

dt_zone: The stop is part of the 50-cent Downtown Fare Zone.

parkride: The bus stop is at a park & ride.

adaaccess: The stop has a firm surface.

busstop_yn: Indicates whether boarding and alighting may occur at a stop. This is used to filter out timepoints and control points used in Metro Transit Scheduling.

IsSuspended: The stop has been suspended temporarily but indefinitely from use in schedules. It will be flagged for installers to apply a “suspended” decal without removing the sign, if one is present.

node_id: For those sites that are nodes, this field contains their four letter identification. Nodes are often timepoints, or places where the bus has to arrive/depart at a certain time. Note, however, that more than one site can have the same Nodeid because a route will use different sites in different directions.

gate: The gate letter or number used for distinguishing stops at specific areas.

T_Code: Transit code TxBase facility identifier. There are cases where stops are associated with a facility. This identifier establishes the relationship between the stop and the facility.

UNIQUE_ID: the street identification number the stop is localized on. Numbers match the road centerlines served on the MN Geospatial Commons, which has adopted the GAC standard. Please note that some IDs are custom HASTUS generated during street adjustment process.

board_flag: this flag indicates if any bus trip allows boarding at the stop. 0 = No; 1 = Yes

alight_flag: this flag indicates if any bus trip allows alighting at the stop. 0 = No; 1 = Yes

active_status: indicates whether stop is active or archived. Active is defined as an available stop for Metro Transit scheduling department. Archived defined as stop that has been eliminated indefinitely for schedules.

itinerary_yn: indicates whether a stops is part of Service Week's active itinerary. Itinerary is defined as the route/path taken from one stop to the next stop.

route_provider: indicates the line provider that serves the stop. Metro Transit trumps other providers if there are multiple providers servicing the stop. Met Council trumps other providers besides Metro Transit if there are multiple providers servicing a stop. Therefore, if just Metro Transit and just Met Council appear as value, it does not mean the sole provider for that stop.
